items: Deleting a worktree directory with rm -rf. Root cause: the entry under .git/worktrees/ remains and keeps its claim on the branch until git worktree prune.
git worktree add ../name to "copy what I have". Root cause: with only a path, Git creates a new branch named after the last path component.
git stash pop in a repository with several worktrees. Root cause: refs/stash is under refs/ and therefore shared; the newest entry may belong to another task.

slides.lead: Let's land this. You should now be able to say:
items: A stopped rebase stays intact while I fix something in another worktree, because the rebase state is per worktree and the new branch is a shared ref.
For review I add a detached worktree at the remote-tracking branch, or name the branch if I will push to it.
I remove worktrees with git worktree remove, clean up after manual deletion with prune, and after manual moves with repair.
Ignored files are not in a new worktree; the stash list, the configuration and the hooks are shared by all of them.
When I need isolation, I use a separate clone.

slides.body: Read sections 25.5 to 25.10 of Chapter 25 and do the Practice section, 25.12.
Today you fixed production without giving up a half-finished rebase, and you know the seven verbs of a worktree's life.

beats.text: "Production rejects nothing when the question is empty and the retriever falls over. I need a fix in ten minutes."
beats.tele: "Production rejects nothing when the question is empty and the retriever falls over. I need a fix in ten minutes."

beats.text: You're in the middle of a rebase, the command that replays your commits onto a new base. It stopped at a conflict, and you've already resolved two earlier ones by hand. You type git switch main. Refused. You type git stash. It fails, because an index with unmerged entries can't be written as a tree.
beats.tele: You're in the middle of a rebase, the command that replays your commits onto a new base. It stopped at a conflict, and you've already resolved two earlier ones by hand. You type `git switch main`. Refused. You type `git stash`. It fails, because an index with unmerged entries can't be written as a tree.

beats.text: Three options are left. Abort the rebase and throw away the resolutions you've done. Clone the repository a second time and wait for the download. Or read the second line of Git's own error message, which says: Consider "git rebase --quit" or "git worktree add".
beats.tele: Three options are left. Abort the rebase and throw away the resolutions you've done. Clone the repository a second time and wait for the download. Or read the second line of Git's own error message, which says: Consider "git rebase --quit" or "git worktree add".

beats.text: Welcome back to Git and GitHub Deep Mastery. Pull up a chair. Last time you learned what a linked worktree is on disk, a second working tree with its own HEAD and index on the same repository, and why one branch can be checked out in only one of them.

beats.text: Why a worktree solves the hotfix. The state of a rebase lives in .git/rebase-merge/, and that is per worktree. Nothing that happens in another worktree can disturb it. On screen, the first worktree of today's demo: a conflict in the file, unmerged entries in the index, a detached HEAD.
beats.tele: Why a worktree solves the hotfix. The state of a rebase lives in `.git/rebase-merge/`, and that is per worktree. Nothing that happens in another worktree can disturb it. On screen, the first worktree of today's demo: a conflict in the file, unmerged entries in the index, a detached HEAD.

beats.text: The hotfix branch, on the other hand, is an ordinary shared ref. It starts at main, it gets the fix as a commit, and it's still there after its worktree is gone.
beats.tele: The hotfix branch, on the other hand, is an ordinary shared ref. It starts at `main`, it gets the fix as a commit, and it's still there after its worktree is gone.

beats.text: Reviewing. A detached worktree at a remote-tracking branch, your record of a branch on the server, gives you the files to read, run and test, without creating a local branch that you would have to delete later. If you intend to push commits to the branch, name it instead: when no local branch of that name exists and exactly one remote has one, git worktree add creates a tracking branch, the same convenience that git switch offers.
beats.tele: Reviewing. A detached worktree at a remote-tracking branch, your record of a branch on the server, gives you the files to read, run and test, without creating a local branch that you would have to delete later. If you intend to push commits to the branch, name it instead: when no local branch of that name exists and exactly one remote has one, `git worktree add` creates a tracking branch, the same convenience that `git switch` offers.

beats.text: Parallel work. Each task gets a branch and a directory. Compared with separate clones, the worktrees share one object database, so a branch committed in one directory can be diffed, merged or cherry-picked from any other immediately. The one-branch rule gives each person or agent exclusive ownership of its branch.
beats.tele: Parallel work. Each task gets a branch and a directory. Compared with separate clones, the worktrees share one object database, so a branch committed in one directory can be diffed, merged or cherry-picked from any other immediately. The one-branch rule gives each person or agent exclusive ownership of its branch.

beats.text: What you supply yourself: dependencies and build output for each worktree. Separate ports, caches and local databases. An instruction never to stash. Integration, which is still a merge. And cleanup.
beats.tele: What you supply yourself: dependencies and build output for each worktree. Separate ports, caches and local databases. An instruction never to stash. Integration, which is still a merge. And cleanup.

beats.text: The life cycle. git worktree add has three common forms. A path only: Git creates a new branch named after the last path component, starting at HEAD. That default surprises people who meant "give me a copy of what I have". With -b, an explicit new branch and a starting point. With --detach, no branch at all.
beats.tele: The life cycle. `git worktree add` has three common forms. A path only: Git creates a new branch named after the last path component, starting at HEAD. That default surprises people who meant "give me a copy of what I have". With `-b`, an explicit new branch and a starting point. With `--detach`, no branch at all.

beats.text: 🟡 CAUTION: git worktree remove deletes the working tree directory and its entry under .git/worktrees/, including its HEAD reflog. It refuses when the tree has modified or untracked files. Removing a worktree doesn't delete its branch.
beats.tele: 🟡 CAUTION: `git worktree remove` deletes the working tree directory and its entry under `.git/worktrees/`, including its HEAD reflog. It refuses when the tree has modified or untracked files. Removing a worktree doesn't delete its branch.

beats.text: git worktree lock protects a worktree from prune, move and remove. git worktree move relocates a linked worktree and updates both pointers. It can't move the main worktree, nor a worktree that contains submodules.
beats.tele: `git worktree lock` protects a worktree from prune, move and remove. `git worktree move` relocates a linked worktree and updates both pointers. It can't move the main worktree, nor a worktree that contains submodules.

beats.text: If someone removes the directory with rm -rf, the entry remains, and with it the claim on the branch. 🟡 CAUTION: git worktree prune removes such entries. If the directory was moved with mv, one of the two pointers is stale, and git worktree repair, which is 🟢 SAFE, rewrites them.
beats.tele: If someone removes the directory with `rm -rf`, the entry remains, and with it the claim on the branch. 🟡 CAUTION: `git worktree prune` removes such entries. If the directory was moved with `mv`, one of the two pointers is stale, and `git worktree repair`, which is 🟢 SAFE, rewrites them.

beats.text: The pitfalls of sharing. Ignored files don't come along: a worktree is a checkout of a commit. Stashes are shared: refs/stash is under refs/. Configuration and hooks are shared: git config set without a scope writes .git/config, which every worktree reads. Per-worktree configuration needs an extension that has to be switched on first.
beats.tele: The pitfalls of sharing. Ignored files don't come along: a worktree is a checkout of a commit. Stashes are shared: `refs/stash` is under `refs/`. Configuration and hooks are shared: `git config set` without a scope writes `.git/config`, which every worktree reads. Per-worktree configuration needs an extension that has to be switched on first.

beats.text: When not to use a worktree. Section 25.9 lists four cases. For a two-minute look at another branch when your working tree is clean: git switch is enough. To get isolation: worktrees share refs, stashes, configuration and hooks, so for an untrusted experiment, a destructive history rewrite you want to rehearse, or a different set of remotes and credentials, use a separate clone.
beats.tele: When not to use a worktree. Section 25.9 lists four cases. For a two-minute look at another branch when your working tree is clean: `git switch` is enough. To get isolation: worktrees share refs, stashes, configuration and hooks, so for an untrusted experiment, a destructive history rewrite you want to rehearse, or a different set of remotes and credentials, use a separate clone.

beats.text: For a superproject with submodules, unless you have tested your exact workflow: the manual advises against it. And as a substitute for branches: ten worktrees on ten stale branches are ten stale branches.
beats.tele: For a superproject with submodules, unless you have tested your exact workflow: the manual advises against it. And as a substitute for branches: ten worktrees on ten stale branches are ten stale branches.

beats.text: Keep the library with several desks. Today's additions are about the furniture.
beats.tele: Keep the library with several desks. Today's additions are about the furniture.

beats.text: A desk can be added and taken away without touching the shelves. Taking a desk away doesn't un-shelve the books written at it, as long as they were catalogued under a branch. But notes that lay on the desk and were never shelved, the untracked and modified files, go with the desk if you insist.
beats.tele: A desk can be added and taken away without touching the shelves. Taking a desk away doesn't un-shelve the books written at it, as long as they were catalogued under a branch. But notes that lay on the desk and were never shelved, the untracked and modified files, go with the desk if you insist.

beats.text: The library keeps a register of its desks. If a desk is carried out of the building without telling the librarian, the register still lists it and still reserves its branch. That is "prunable".
beats.tele: The library keeps a register of its desks. If a desk is carried out of the building without telling the librarian, the register still lists it and still reserves its branch. That is "prunable".

beats.text: And three things sit at the front counter, not at any desk: the stash drawer, the house rules, and the hooks. Every desk uses the same ones. The analogy breaks if you take it to mean that the desks are independent copies. They aren't, and deleting the main worktree's directory deletes the repository for all of them.

The analogy breaks if you take it to mean that the desks are independent copies. They aren't, and deleting the main worktree's directory deletes the repository for all of them.

beats.text: Both escape routes are closed, and the refusal of git switch names the alternative. 🟢 SAFE: git worktree add -b creates a directory, an entry and a new branch.
beats.tele: Both escape routes are closed, and the refusal of `git switch` names the alternative. 🟢 SAFE: `git worktree add -b` creates a directory, an entry and a new branch.

beats.text: -b creates the branch at main and checks it out in the new directory. The list shows the main worktree as "(detached HEAD)": that is the rebase, which works on a detached HEAD until it finishes.
